subject: Mutual Action Plan: hosting gating, geo commitment & audit items
messages:
From: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@helixhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@helixhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: hosting gating, geo commitment & audit items

Jonas — thanks for the call earlier. Attached is the MAP template we discussed; Raj and I captured our expected timeline and a few compliance asks. Two quick points we need clarity on before we finalize: 

1) Data residency: for the pilot (POC) we need US-only data residency (no cross-border processing). Can Redwood commit to hosted instances in a US region with SOC2 evidence?

2) Deployment mode: our infra team prefers Dedicated for predictable latency, but procurement has concerns about minimums/cost. Can you outline a short ramp plan from Hosted -> Dedicated, and where Private (on‑prem) would even be considered?

Also looping in legal in a follow-up. Can we get a one‑page summary of the three paths (hosted / dedicated / private) with key tradeoffs and acceptance gates by EOD Wed?

Thanks,
Alice
Director, Product & Integrations
HelixHealth

Attachments: HelixHealth_MAP_draft.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@helixhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: hosting gating, geo commitment & audit items

Alice — appreciate the MAP draft and the clarity on the residency constraint. High level answers up front, then I added a proposed MAP milestone table in the attached file (Redwood_MAP_v2.xlsx).

Quick summary: 
- Hosted (fastest onramp): US-region hosted API (we can pin to us‑west / us‑east), SOC2 + encrypted at rest/transport. Good for quick POC in 1–2 weeks with sample data (no upfront capacity commitment).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): reserved GPU pool, predictable latency & throughput, tenant isolation. Typical lead time 4–6 weeks to reserve and provision; we can offer a staged ramp (small commit for month 1–2, scale after acceptance).
- Private (VPC/on‑prem): for customers with hard regulatory needs. Longer lead time, requires network/ops coordination, and typically an enterprise contract + installation window (6–12 weeks depending on site).

Acceptance gates I propose to include in the MAP: POC acceptance (functional), latency SLA for key endpoints, SOC2 evidence & penetration test result, and data residency confirmation. I attached a one-page tradeoff summary as the first sheet.

Marissa — can you add the rough cost delta bullets (hosted -> dedicated) to sheet 2? Irene — quick confirmation on the SOC2 snapshot (I have the latest PDF; will attach).

Alice / Raj — happy to jump on a 30‑minute session Wed morning to walk through the MAP and answer procurement questions. When works?

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_v2.xlsx, SOC2_snapshot_SEPT2026.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@helixhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: hosting gating, geo commitment & audit items

Adding cost & timeline bullets here per Jon's ask — pulled for the MAP sheet: 

- Hosted: No commit; POC pricing = metered + test credits. Typical POC cost for HelixHealth scale (~10k tokens/day) ~= $600–$1,000 for first 30 days. Turn up: hours.
- Dedicated: starting commit (1/8 cluster equiv) estimated baseline $12k/month; ramp plan: month 1 (trial capacity, 50% commit) -> month 2–3 scale to full commit; operations onboarding 2–4 weeks after contract sign.
- Private: license + install; typical T&M + initial infra sizing (~$50–80k one-time) + recurring support license.

Operational notes: for Dedicated we can set a canary fallback to Hosted for overflow to avoid dropped requests during spikes (configurable in MAP). That keeps service continuous during ramp.

Irene — attaching the SOC2 snapshot and the runbook excerpt for region pinning.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2_snapshot_SEPT2026.pdf

From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@helixhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@helixhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: hosting gating, geo commitment & audit items

Thanks team — that makes sense and helps a lot. A couple of action items from our side so we can lock timelines: 

- Legal wants to see a proposed ramp schedule and a sample commitment term for Dedicated (we're comfortable with a 3‑month initial ramp; please include cancellation windows).
- Security: SOC2 snapshot looks good; can you confirm if penetration test reports can be redacted for IP and shared under NDA?
- Ops: we'll trial a Hosted POC (US region) first week of Oct. If latency and quality are acceptable, we intend to move to Dedicated starting mid‑Oct following the MAP acceptance gate.

Can Redwood produce the dedicated ramp schedule + sample TOS (redacted) by EOD Fri so legal can start review? If yes, we'll schedule the Wed AM session now for 9am PT to do a MAP walkthrough.

Raj
VP, Infrastructure
HelixHealth
